newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran minister in Turkey amid growing tension.
newsitem.headline: Iran minister in Turkey amid growing tension.

text.p: Iran's deputy foreign minister, Alaeddin Boroujerdi, has arrived in Ankara amid increasing tension between the two neighbours following Turkey's month-long incursion into northern Iraq.
"He brought a message from (Iranian President Hashemi) Rafsanjani to President Suleyman Demirel," a Turkish foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters.
"We do not know what the message says at the moment. He is expected to meet Demirel later (on Tuesday)," the spokesman said.

The Turkish military has accused Iran, among other countries, of supplying separatist rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party with sophisticated anti-aircraft missiles used to shoot down two Turkish army helicopters.
Iran has publically denied the accusations.
"We want to have good ties with Iran. As a neighbour countries, both have interests in that. But Turkey's security concerns must be resolved," the spokesman said.
In Tehran, Boroujerdi stressed the need for protecting the territorial integrity of Iraq before leaving for Turkey, Iran's state news agency said in a report monitored by the BBC.
Turkey's prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, challenged the secularist establishment by promoting closer ties with Iran since coming to power a year ago.
Erbakan, already at odds with the military over Islamic activism, was accused by the military last week of holding back funding for the northern Iraq operation.
"We have got very close to the Iranian border. It is a very sensitive area. We must be very careful," the daily Sabah quoted Erbakan as telling the army's chief of staff on Monday.
Turkish troops, backed by air power, are understood to be close to Iran's border with the Kurdish-held areas of Iraq. The region, however, remains closed to all journalists.
